title: Deterministic exact-SHA post-merge verification
description: Remediate the first canonical merge regression where a merge performed by GitHub Actions with GITHUB_TOKEN does not emit recursive push-triggered Canonical CI / Phase A runs. The merge executor must bind post-merge verification to the exact merge commit SHA returned by the merged pull request, then run canonical verification plus Phase A in a separate least-privilege GitHub-hosted job bound to that immutable SHA.

external_gate_evidence.rule: All structured gate evidence must bind to the exact current artifact hash. HIGH requires independent Review PASS, Security PASS, explicit Project Owner Human Approval, and ACTIVE lock evidence before merge eligibility.

acceptance_criteria.description: The deterministic merge executor resolves the exact merge_commit_sha from the merged PR in the workflow's canonical repository after the merge API succeeds and rejects missing, unmerged, malformed, or non-resolvable canonical commit state.

Post-merge verification checks out the exact resolved merge SHA from github.repository, verifies the checkout binding, persists no Git credentials, and never relies on moving main, PR-head, github.ref, or github.sha for test execution.
The post-merge verifier runs full pnpm verify and Phase A verification against the exact merged commit with PostgreSQL available.
No Ruleset relaxation, no direct-main mutation, and no change to Canonical CI or Phase A verifier semantics is introduced.
The observed first-canonical-merge regression is recorded with exact run and merge evidence and remains fail-visible until this remediation is canonical and exercised by a later canonical merge.

Trust boundary remains canonical-repository-only: the existing Merge Policy Controller rejects external head repositories before merge, and post-merge checkout explicitly uses github.repository plus the canonical PR's resolved merge SHA rather than a fork or PR-head reference.

Post-merge code execution is isolated from merge-write credentials by running in a separate GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest job with contents:read only and persist-credentials:false; no PAT or GitHub App token is introduced. The job is not claimed to be a no-code-execution sandbox: repository verification intentionally executes reviewed canonical code, the workspace is writable, and default GitHub-hosted network access is not restricted by this task.

If exact-SHA post-merge verification is not successful after merge, the workflow remains failed/visible and a separate issues:write reporter job creates or reuses an Owner-assigned POST_MERGE_FAILED investigation issue. Automatic rollback is prohibited; rollback requires a new governed decision/task.

Race safety is immutable-SHA based: later movement of main cannot retarget an in-flight verification because the verifier consumes only needs.merge.outputs.merge_sha; each later canonical merge receives its own workflow_dispatch execution and exact merge SHA.

Credential scope is least-privilege per job: merge uses only the per-run GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN with contents:write/pull-requests:write; postmerge verification has contents:read only and no persisted Git credentials; failure reporting uses a separate per-run token with issues:write only for incident creation/Owner assignment. No persistent PAT or repository secret is added.

Post-merge verification has a 30-minute job timeout and failure reporting has a 5-minute timeout. Token Telemetry remains NOT_IMPLEMENTED until frozen implementation Item 7; native GitHub Actions timing/log evidence is not mislabeled as Item 7 telemetry.
